main_text.p: .19. sic dicit, καὶ αὐτὸς[?], οὗς scilicet ἐνεργη-τικὸς, καὶ ἀμιγὴς, καὶ ἀπαθής, & paulò post addit, καὶ τὸ μόνον ἀδύνατον καὶ ἰδίον: quanquam quid Aristoteli sit τῆς ἐνεργητικῆς[?], non ita perspicuum est; sed quicquid sit de ejus sententia, quod anima rationalis à corpore separata & seorsim existere possit probari solet à Physicis ex ejus actionibus; cujus enim rei actiones non pendent à corpore, idipsum non pendet à corpore: ut enim se habent operationes rei ad materiam, ita se etiam habet existentia: at animæ operationes, puta intelligere & velle, non pendent à corpore, seu non exercentur per corpus, ut visus, auditus &c. ergo animæ substantia est immaterialis, ac proinde extra corpus potest existere.

II. Hoc constituto, declarandum porrò, quæ sit natura animæ separatæ, quæ proprietates, quæ actiones, & quæ diversitas, quæ tamen obscura sunt ob id, quod animarum separatarum nulla sentiamus effecta: interim ex iis quæ de Angelis dixi, quæque in Physicis docentur de actionibus animæ in corpore, quodammodo colligo conditionem & statum animarum separatarum. Primò ergo statuimus, animam rationalem esse partem humanæ essentiæ, non totum hominem, ut Plato voluit; corpus enim ad essentiam hominis pertinet haud dubiè; alias enim cum anima separatur à corpore, non potest dici homo mori aut

page.notes: The Greek words in the first paragraph were read at a small size and are uncertain; the first Greek word and the Greek after "quanquam quid Aristoteli sit" are marked [?]. The initial ".19." is a paragraph number and is kept as printed. The first paragraph is marked as a continuation from the previous page because its first line is not indented. The printed "corpore;" and "feorfim" are kept as read and normalised only for long s and u/v. "P 4" is the signature and "aut" the catchword.
